title: A Chair for Everyone
passage:
The art room at Takumi's school had twenty-four stools and two regular chairs. Most students used the stools without thinking about them. During an open class, however, a visitor with an injured leg found it difficult to sit safely. The teacher brought one of the regular chairs, but it was stored in another room and took time to find.

After the event, the class discussed whether the art room needed different seating. Buying twenty-four new chairs would be expensive and unnecessary. The stools were useful because they could be stacked and moved easily. Instead, the students tried to understand what kinds of situations required another option. They asked the school nurse and spoke with students who had temporarily used crutches after sports injuries.

They learned that a backrest was helpful for some people, and armrests could make standing up easier. Space was also important because a large chair placed between crowded art tables might create a new problem. The class decided to keep most stools and add three stable chairs with backs. One chair also had armrests. They marked a small storage area so the chairs would always be easy to find.

A few months later, one student hurt her ankle and used one of the chairs for two weeks. Another student sometimes chose a chair because of back pain. The chairs were not reserved only for people with visible injuries. The teacher explained that anyone who needed a different seat could use one without having to give a long reason.

Takumi found that the room still looked almost the same. There had been no large renovation, yet the space worked better for more people. He learned that making a place accessible does not always mean replacing everything with one ‘perfect’ design. Sometimes variety is more useful. Different people, and even the same person on different days, may need different things. A room can become more welcoming simply by offering more than one way to use it.
translation:
タクミの学校の美術室には、二十四脚の丸椅子と普通の椅子が二脚ありました。普段は誰も気にしませんでしたが、公開授業の日、足をけがした来場者が安全に座りにくい場面がありました。先生が別室から背もたれ付きの椅子を持ってきましたが、探すのに時間がかかりました。

授業後、すべての椅子を買い替える必要があるのか話し合いました。丸椅子は積み重ねられ移動しやすい利点があります。そこで、どんな時に別の座席が必要なのかを保健室や松葉杖を使った経験のある生徒へ聞きました。

背もたれが役立つ人がいること、立ち上がる際にひじ掛けが助けになる場合があること、そして大きな椅子を狭い机の間へ置くと別の問題が生まれることが分かりました。そこで丸椅子は残し、背もたれ付きの安定した椅子を三脚追加し、そのうち一脚にはひじ掛けを付けました。保管位置も決め、いつでも見つけられるようにしました。

数か月後、足首を痛めた生徒が二週間利用し、腰痛のある生徒も時々使いました。目に見えるけがの人だけの専用品にはせず、必要なら長い説明をしなくても使えるようにしました。

美術室の見た目はほとんど変わっていませんが、より多くの人が使いやすくなりました。利用しやすい空間を作ることは、すべてを一つの『完璧な形』へ変えることではない場合があります。人によって、また同じ人でも日によって必要なものは違います。複数の使い方を用意するだけで、場所はより受け入れやすくなるのです。
